title: The friend who went quiet
old_caption: When a friend goes quiet, it is easy to assume it is about you. Often it isn't. Send a check-in with no homework attached: thinking of you, no need to reply.

title: Check-in, not a quiz
old_caption: Six questions in a row can feel like a test, even when they come from love. Ask one soft question, then let the quiet do some of the work. Save this for the next time you're worried about a friend.

title: December is hard for some friends
old_caption: Not everyone loves this month, especially in a year when someone is missing. You don't have to fix it. Ask if they want company or quiet, and make room for both.

title: The plan you can say no to
old_caption: The kindest invites come with an easy way out. Pyjamas welcome, leave whenever, no is totally fine. When saying no is easy, saying yes gets a little easier too.

title: The cancelled-plans friend
old_caption: Third cancellation and the scorecard is already drafted. Skip it. Say how it felt once, kindly, then ask what's going on with them. Sometimes the answer is just: I'm overbooked.

title: Long-distance friends
old_caption: Different cities, different clocks, a lot of missed calls. A small ritual beats a perfect plan: one time, every week, kept. Who would you set a standing call with?

title: Who checks on the checker?
old_caption: The friend who always listens rarely gets asked how they are. Turn the question around tonight, and then actually wait for the answer. Tag the friend who holds everyone up.

title: Show up with soup
old_caption: When a friend is sick, the best care asks nothing back. Leave the soup at the door, send one line, and let them rest without having to host you.

title: Good news, shared
old_caption: Hiding good news to protect a struggling friend can leave them out of something lovely. Friends can hold both. Share it gently and let them choose to celebrate with you.

title: When a friend is in a new relationship
old_caption: A friend in love can disappear for a while. "You've changed" pushes them away; "we miss you" invites them back. Say it warmly, and leave room for the new person too.
